input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console. Cluster administrators can see, for each data science project, which workbenches are sitting idle: each entry shows the workbench's last activity, its owner, and the resources it reserves (volumes, CPU, memory). The report is sourced from the notebook controller's existing activity tracking — no new data collection is built. Administrators can export the report as CSV.

## Scope

- A new report view in the web console, organized per project, listing workbenches considered idle
- Per-workbench columns: last activity timestamp (from the notebook controller's activity tracking), owner, reserved resources
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report for administrators
- Read-only reporting only — no reclamation or deletion actions (out of scope per the strategy)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing recent activity, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then the report lists the idle workbenches with each one's last activity, owner, and reserved resources.
- The last-activity values displayed in the report match the notebook controller's activity tracking for a sampled set of workbenches (validates the passive notebook-controller data source).
- Given the idle-workbench report, when an administrator exports it as CSV, then a CSV file is downloaded containing the same rows and columns as the displayed report.
- The report offers no automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources, and performs no cost or chargeback calculation (out-of-scope guard).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. Fully covered by this epic.
- **HLR-3 (P2)** — CSV export of this report. Bundled here rather than split: the export edits the same report UI surface and data the P1 work builds, so splitting would double-touch the same surface.

# Stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console. Cluster administrators can see completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age that still retain their artifacts, so they can identify runs whose accumulated storage is reclaimable. The report is sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines' retained run-completion metadata — no new data collection is built. Administrators can export the report as CSV.

## Scope

- A new report view in the web console, organized per project, listing completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold
- Per-run information: completion time and retained artifacts
- A configurable age threshold that administrators can adjust to control which runs count as stale
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report for administrators
- Read-only reporting only — no reclamation or deletion actions (out of scope per the strategy)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing completed pipeline runs of differing ages, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report for that project, then runs completed earlier than the configured age threshold are listed with their completion time and retained artifacts.
- Given a change to the configurable age threshold, when the report is viewed again, then the set of listed runs reflects the new threshold.
- The run completion data displayed in the report matches Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata for a sampled set of runs (validates the passive pipelines data source).
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator exports it as CSV, then a CSV file is downloaded containing the same rows and columns as the displayed report.
- The report offers no automated reclamation or deletion of runs or artifacts, and performs no cost or chargeback calculation (out-of-scope guard).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. Fully covered by this epic.
- **HLR-3 (P2)** — CSV export of this report. Bundled here rather than split: the export edits the same report UI surface and data the P1 work builds, so splitting would double-touch the same surface.

# Documentation for the idle and stale resource reports

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the two new administrator reports in the RHOAI web console — the per-project idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run report — and the safe reclamation steps administrators can take based on them. It is authored after the reports are implemented so the content describes what was actually built.

## Scope

Content outline:

- A documentation topic explaining the idle-workbench report: what it shows (last activity, owner, reserved resources), where its data comes from (notebook controller activity tracking), and how to interpret it per project
- A documentation topic explaining the stale pipeline-run report: what it shows (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), how to configure the age threshold, and how to interpret it
- Guidance on safe manual reclamation steps administrators can take using each report (deleting stale artifacts, resizing or removing idle workbenches), including cautions consistent with the strategy's out-of-scope statement (no automated reclamation)
- Coverage of the CSV export capability for both reports

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation topics explain both reports, the configurable stale-age threshold, and the CSV export capability.
- The documentation includes safe reclamation steps that are consistent with the implemented reports and recommends no automated reclamation or deletion (which is out of scope).
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports by the feature team, and any inaccuracies found in review are corrected before publication.
- The documentation claims no capability the reports do not have (no cost/chargeback, no automated reclamation).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. Fully covered by this epic.
